title: Man killed by police had gun, crystal meth
article: The Saskatoon man who was shot and killed by police last year was carrying a high-powered handgun and was likely high on crystal meth, a coroner's inquest heard Tuesday.
Andrew Moore died April 30, 2004, in a Saskatoon confectionary after a scuffle with a police officer.
Const. Tim Bayly, the Saskatoon Police Service officer who fatally shot Moore, told the inquest he was trying to arrest Moore on a warrant.
Bayly remembered Moore from a past run-in as tense, paranoid and likely concealing a weapon.
As Bayly tried to make the arrest, Moore ran into a nearby store.
He caught up to Moore at the back of the building. They struggled, and when Bayly saw Moore with a gun pointed at him, he shot him in the face.
Police investigators found Moore was carrying a .357 Magnum snub-nosed revolver loaded with six bullets. He had 44 more bullets in his fanny pack and was carrying a leather club-like device.
Police found a small plastic vial in his pocket that had residue of the street drug crystal meth.
There was also crystal meth in Moore's blood and urine samples.
